name: Alice's sister
timbre: warm, soft, smooth young woman's voice, gently rounded, a little low for her age, calm and unhurried
pitch: medium-high mezzo-soprano, settled and even, small intonation swings
accent: Received Pronunciation of an educated upper-middle-class English girl: soft, clear, refined, no regional features
reference_style: The only fully waking adult-ish voice: kind authority, indulgent 'dear', never raised. Must be clearly older, lower and slower than Alice so the two sisters never blur. Glimpsed silently at the trial (ruling 5.3 B) — no dream-side lines.

waking_call.note: ch012-d0063 'Wake up, Alice dear!' — bright but gentle, never a shout

reverie_murmur.note: any designed lines in her closing reverie (ev0054); dreamy, half to herself

voice_evidence.quote: “Wake up, Alice dear!” said her sister

reason: The source never describes her voice; designed from personality ('Never uses force or raised-voice authority') and the household class (h1_summary §1).
